label: At D2 high after common a1->S1, low after common a2->S2; D1 high after unrewarded S2.
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == S1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == S2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == S1) ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 6. GO is near saturation (~+0.95) and carries almost no information. At D2 the magnitude is set by the choice x reached-state combination just observed: about +0.7 above timing for common a1->S1, about -0.5 for common a2->S2, with the rare transitions in between (a2->S1 near baseline, a1->S2 somewhat low). At D1 it rises after an unrewarded trial that reached S2 (+0.4) and falls after a rewarded S1 trial. The free fit adds the D1 drop after rewarded S1 and a small D2 drop when the previous trial was rewarded. The observer belief adds nothing once the transition is in the model; its apparent D2 effect is just the reached state. No future variables used.

issues: The D2 part holds up. Profile residuals by this trial's choice x state at D2: a1S1 +0.69, a1S2 -0.29, a2S1 +0.04, a2S2 -0.52, which matches the explanation (rare transitions in between, a1->S2 somewhat low). An additive D2 model of state plus action scores the same on its own (0.737 test for S1, S2 and a1 terms vs 0.731 for a1S1, a2S2 and invalid), so the 'common a1->S1 / common a2->S2' wording is fine and is not curve fitting.

The D1 claim is incomplete. D1 residuals by previous trial: a1S2u +0.33, a2S2u +0.42, a1S1u +0.09, a2S1u +0.08, a1S1r -0.28, a2S1r -0.20, S2r about 0. That is roughly additive: reaching S2 raises it and reward lowers it. The label mentions only 'high after unrewarded S2', so a reader cannot predict the drop after rewarded S1, which the explanation itself admits.

Running misses on the recorded short form leaves a systematic D1 error class: over-predicted after a1 S1 r (-0.239) and a2 S1 r (-0.162), under-predicted after a1 S1 u (+0.131) and a2 S1 u (+0.120). The worst windows are long late-episode streaks of rewarded a1->S1 trials. There D1 sits at -0.45 to -0.6 against a prediction of +0.06, and D2 sits near 0.0-0.15 against +0.22. So a reward-streak effect at D1 is not captured.

The D1 term's specificity to S2 is not supported. Replacing (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S2) * (prev_reward == 0) with the simpler (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) scores slightly better on test (0.8105 vs 0.8068). Its misses still leave D1 errors of about 0.15-0.22 (after a2 S2 u +0.179, after a1 S1 r -0.221). Under the three-factor limit, no single D1 term captures both the S2 effect and the reward effect.

Most belief claims hold: (phase == D2) * belief_lo adds only +0.002 to the free fit (0.8087), and adding (phase == D2) * (state == S1) * (prev_reward == 1) adds nothing. One correction: (phase == D1) * belief_lo adds +0.026 (0.8326) and (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) adds +0.019. So belief and reward carry real extra D1 information, even though belief alone as the D1 term is worse (0.738).

The overall fit is high (test R^2 beyond timing 0.807, against 0.91 for all observed cues), and the D2 description is accurate. The evidence is mixed because the D1 description misses a sizeable, systematic part of the signal: the reward-driven drop, which is strongest during rewarded S1 streaks.
